title: Economy model (.gamestudio/economy/*.economy.json)
description: A Machinations-style resource-flow model that economy_sim.py runs as a Monte Carlo simulation over player archetypes: resources (pools with caps), nodes (sources, sinks, converters, gates, pools) fired by triggers, a level difficulty curve, purchasable offers and the targets the sim checks. Resource ids should match contract economy.currencies ids.

trigger.description: When a node fires: per_session (session start), per_minute (of play), per_level_attempt, per_level_win, per_level_loss, daily (first session of a day), weekly, on_purchase (after an offer is bought), on_ad (after a rewarded ad is watched).

name.description: Optional model name/version label, e.g. "v1 soft-launch baseline".

days.description: Simulated horizon in days (economy_sim.py --days overrides). 30-90 covers early-game balance; use 180+ for content-runway questions.

archetypes.description: Player archetypes simulated in parallel; shares should sum to 1.0.

items.description: A player archetype: behaviour parameters for the simulator.

share.description: Share of the player population (all shares sum to 1.0).

skill.description: Relative skill 0-1; 0.5 plays at the designed base_win_rate, higher wins more often.

spend_propensity.description: Probability of buying an offer when its trigger fires.

ad_accept_rate.description: Probability of accepting an optional rewarded ad when offered.

items.description: One resource and its starting state.

id.description: Resource id, e.g. "coins"; node inputs/outputs and offer contents use it.

initial.description: Starting balance for a new player.

cap.description: Maximum balance (overflow is lost and reported), or null for uncapped.

nodes.description: Flow nodes. A node fires on its trigger, with optional probability and condition, consuming inputs and producing outputs.

kind.description: source (creates resources from nothing), sink (destroys them), converter (inputs to outputs), gate (fires only when inputs are affordable / condition holds, e.g. unlocks), pool (accumulates for later release, e.g. a piggy bank).

inputs.description: Resources consumed per firing; the node is skipped when the player cannot afford them.

probability.description: Chance the node fires when triggered (default 1.0). Use it for drop rates and voluntary behaviour such as spending.

condition.description: Optional guard expression, e.g. "day >= 2" or "stars >= 3". Keep to comparisons of resource ids and simulator variables (day, level, session) joined by and/or; economy_sim.py defines the exact grammar it evaluates.

levels.description: Level progression used by the per_level_* triggers.

base_win_rate.description: First-attempt win rate of an average-skill player before the difficulty curve applies.

difficulty_curve.description: Shape of difficulty over levels (difficulty_curve.py generates and analyses these).

params.description: Curve parameters, e.g. {"base": 0.85, "floor": 0.45, "period": 10, "hard_every": 10} matching difficulty_curve.py options, or {"win_rates": [...]} for custom.

offers.description: Purchasable offers the simulator may present.

id.description: Offer id; should match a contract monetization.iap id.

trigger.description: When the offer is shown: a node trigger name (e.g. "per_level_loss") or a condition such as "level >= 6".

targets.description: Health targets the simulation is checked against.

days_to_complete_content.description: Days a median engaged player should need to finish all levels; shorter means content runs out.

max_soft_currency_hoard_days.description: Soft currency balance should never exceed this many days of typical income; larger hoards mean sinks are too weak.

payer_conversion.description: Expected share of players who buy at least once over the horizon.
